post.caption:
Sleep is four stages, cycling about every 90 minutes, five times a night. Light sleep, then deep slow-wave sleep for physical repair and memory consolidation, then REM, where the brain looks awake and the body is paralysed so you cannot act the dream out. The mix is not even: deep sleep is front-loaded into the first half, REM grows towards morning. Which is why cutting the last two hours costs you most of your dreaming.
